title: The Rocket and the Referee
setup: March 1955. Boston's Hal Laycoe hits Montreal star Maurice Richard with a high stick, and Laycoe is penalized. Richard attacks Laycoe with his stick. When referee Cliff Thompson steps in, Richard punches him in the face twice. Three days later, NHL president Clarence Campbell rules on Richard.
question: What does Campbell decide?
options: A suspension for the rest of the regular season and the playoffs
A fine only, with the playoffs open to him
ruling: On March 16, 1955, Campbell suspended Richard for the rest of the regular season and the playoffs. The next night, at a Red Wings-Canadiens game in Montreal where Campbell was in attendance, fans threw objects and a tear gas bomb went off. The game was cut short and a street riot followed, with 16 arrests and 33 injuries. The next day Richard appeared on television, urged fans to behave and said he would accept his punishment. Montreal won the Stanley Cup the following season.
rulebookNote: The source describes the suspension by length only and cites no rule number.
